category_summaries.summary: The agreement recognizes that the Company and the Union share an interest in harmonious labor relations and agree that employees in specified listed exchanges and geographic areas are governed exclusively by this Labor Agreement. The Company recognizes the Union as the exclusive collective-bargaining representative for covered employees (including, specifically, Verizon North Inc. (North Central Region) under IBEW bargaining unit certification 8-RC-7220) for collective bargaining on rates of pay, hours, and all other conditions of employment. The agreement also addresses Union security/recognition mechanisms: with written employee authorization, the Company deducts and remits Union dues or service fees monthly (beginning the first calendar month after authorization; during the contract term), subject to limits (no deductions for temporary/occasional/probationary employees as specified), equal allocation across two pay periods, and suspension during leave of absence or layoff (with automatic resumption upon return except for military leave or exhausted recall rights). Employees may revoke authorizations in writing, stopping deductions beginning the first calendar month after receipt. The Union indemnifies the Company for claims related to deductions, and an Agency Shop obligation provides that the Union represents all bargaining unit employees fairly and applies during the agreement term; membership is not compulsory, probationary employees may choose union membership (optionally within specified timing), and employees are afforded Service Fee status/requirements where appropriate.

The contract and related memoranda generally set fixed expiration dates and provide for renewal on a year-to-year basis unless terminated by written notice. For example, an agreement binding from 12:01 A.M. October 27, 2002 through October 22, 2005 continues from year to year thereafter until terminated by at least sixty (60) days’ written notice; related memoranda effective October 27, 2002 also expire October 22, 2005, with their specific terms (including Compensated Availability, other benefit terms, and the Mail Order Prescription Plan) terminating on that date and not surviving unless the parties agree in writing. Another memorandum effective December 21, 2002 expires October 22, 2005 on the same “no-survival unless agreed” basis. In other instances, terms continue year to calendar year unless terminated by either party with thirty (30) days’ written notice, or remain in effect through the life of the current agreement subject to thirty (30) days’ written notice. Extensions and timing of obligations may be extended by mutual consent (including extending time limits prior to their expiration), and, separately, probationary periods may be extended by mutual Company-Union agreement for an additional ninety (90) days (with eligibility for holiday allowance under Article 10). The provisions also allow modifications based on legal compliance (including possible rescission) without a duty to bargain in certain circumstances, and allow amendments to some agreements only with notice of at least sixty (60) and not more than ninety (90) days prior to a termination date.

The Agreement preserves broad Management authority over business operations and the direction of the workforce, including hiring, job assignments and tours, equipment/process improvements, combining or discontinuing jobs, setting employee numbers, establishing rules, and disciplining or discharging employees for cause, as well as being the sole judge of service to the public (and clarifying that specific Management functions do not limit other Management functions). Management may recognize and enforce established telephone service and work standards, may not retain employees who fail continuously to meet standards unless caused by conditions beyond their control, and may discipline or discharge employees who repeatedly refuse to meet standards while treating employees fairly and justly. Management must consider extenuating circumstances when overtime employees are unavailable and may direct or require assignments tied to business needs, including assigning employees to Compensated Availability where business needs exist (otherwise voluntary) and replacing employees on leave with temporary or contract workers for the leave duration. Management retains control over supervisory work restrictions (except for emergencies affecting service or safety/health/welfare, instruction, or when no appropriate employee is available), tool specifications, and home dispatch offerings (including determining the individuals/work groups), and it may amend certain plans (including MOPP, including carrier selection) while not diminishing benefits. The Company also administers performance/objectives and standards, can adjust standards with at least 30 days’ notice of goal changes to affected employees and the Union, and Team Performance Award/objectives are not grievable/arbitrable. Operational planning rights include amending product/service procedures with reasonable advance notice and reserving the right to adjust product/service mix and objectives. For staffing and employment administration, Management may fill openings temporarily up to 30 days, reserve rights regarding retention of employees with essential skills, exercise discretion on permitted/alternate relocation locations based on business needs with due weight to employee desires, require return to work on the agreed date (with termination if not returned absent a personal compelling reason as determined by Management), and manage voluntary part-time assignments (total duration not to exceed four months) where management has sole discretion over whether to offer them, their time frame/duration, number, location, and classification, with offerings subject to Management approval and requiring at least 30 days’ discussion/advance notice before implementation. Management may also use other company employees for work normally performed by employees on voluntary layoff leave or voluntary part-time assignments and may set/adjust standards and objectives to ensure equitable treatment.

Compensation provisions provide for bargaining of pay rates for newly established job classifications only if the Union requests within 30 days of notification; the Company’s rate continues in effect until agreement is reached, and agreed rates are not retroactive earlier than the job’s establishment date. Pay premiums include Sunday work at a 1/2 premium (with Sunday hours up to a maximum of 8 or 10 hours counting toward weekly hours in excess of 40), night premium of $0.85/hour for regularly scheduled hours between 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. (excluding overtime hours), and additional differentials such as $0.75/hour for in-charge duty (per hour served), $0.75/hour for Dispatch Clerk designated functions (with no pyramiding), $0.75/hour for Order Clerk coordinating special service circuit orders (no pyramiding), and a $0.75/hour performance differential mechanism (where applicable) that applies only to hours actually worked (including overtime), requires 840 straight-time hours in a 6-month period, continues only until discontinued (with eligibility restrictions after merit increases and 90-day continuation after process suspension), and ends on the employee’s last day paid. Temporary wage protection bars wage reductions when temporarily assigned to a lower-paying job; if temporarily assigned to a higher classification for purposes outside the temporary lower-wage protection, the employee receives the appropriate wage differential under Exhibit A. Overtime is compensated for hours outside the original tour (with straight-time within the tour), and release-time rules can provide up to 4 hours’ pay if an agreement is reached within the first half of the tour (5 hours for 4/10s). Per diem replaces other expenses unless specified; if the temporary reporting center is closer than the regular one, no per diem/mileage is paid (except where required to travel to the regular center first). Per diem/mileage is tiered by distance (e.g., $11/day for 10–20 miles; $21.50/day for >20–40 miles; $36/day for >40–60 miles), and beyond 60 miles the Company provides lodging at the employee’s request plus a $34/day meal allowance, with company-paid initial/last transportation and interim-weekend mileage allowances when personal vehicles are used; for assignments >60 miles outside Ohio, reasonable board/lodging with approval is paid and meals are either receipted or $34/day, with no other per diem. Termination/layment-related allowances require regular employees with 2+ years’ credited service losing employment through layoff to receive a termination allowance calculated as one week (40 hours) per accredited year at the basic wage rate at layoff (prorated for regular part-time based on the prior 13-week average), paid under payroll procedures unless limited to non-conditional lump-sum scenarios, excluding earned vacation; incentive/commission provisions include quarterly commission payment timing, caps/limits on compensated attainment (e.g., performance total attainment capped at 110% unless 100% monthly quota achieved), prorated commission eligibility upon transfer/promotion, mechanisms to adjust future payouts for over/underpayments without requiring repayment from base salary in certain situations, and repayment of fraudulent/inaccurate sales results. Availability and other specialized compensations include an availability program (where established), with compensation of $125/week assignments (including Saturday/Sunday), $15/day for single assignments, and $25 for non-scheduled days, payable only if employees remain available and accessible during the assignment. Additional provisions adjust wages upon job changes using wage-schedule rules (higher schedule immediately above; lower schedule at same or immediately below; same schedule no change) and set minimum wage increases for certain incentives (minimum $0.75/hour), address force-reduction displacement return within 2 years, and provide various specific differentials and ISP termination benefits (including maximum $750 per year up to $3,750, lump-sum payment timing, prorating for part-time, and optional enhanced benefits equal to two times regular at the Company’s discretion).

Scheduling rules provide for how employee tours and overtime are assigned, posted, and adjusted. The Company determines when overtime is worked and gives as much reasonable advance notice as practicable; overtime is paid at one-and-one-half times the straight-time rate with no pyramiding of overtime/premium rates for the same hours, and holiday allowance is credited as time worked for overtime computation (no other paid excused time counts except as expressly provided). Employees generally will not be scheduled to work more than 14 hours in any 24-hour period except where required by service needs; when an employee works 14+ hours in a 24-hour period, they are entitled to 8 consecutive hours off before returning, and if that rest overlaps their regular scheduled hours they receive straight-time for the overlapping hours necessary to complete the 8-hour rest, with the employee able to request to be excused from the remaining balance of the tour without pay for safety/health (no contractual violation). Call-outs outside regular hours are compensated starting from when the employee leaves home through return (with reasonable travel time) and include a weekday minimum of two hours at the overtime rate; if an employee accepts a call-out, they are excused from required overtime once within the next seven scheduled work days if they request an 8-hour scheduled day (10 hours for 4/10s), and if a call-out working 4 hours after midnight prevents sufficient rest before the next scheduled tour, the employee may choose excusal under the seven-day rule or be excused from the first half of the scheduled tour without pay. Regular tours are assigned by seniority according to employees’ written selections, subject to workload, telephone service requirements, and legal requirements; work group schedules are posted every four weeks with opportunity to request tour changes in the week before posting. Employees may trade scheduled hours with supervisor approval, but approval is ordinarily denied if the trade results in overtime. Posted schedules may change for reasons beyond the Company’s control: if at least 24 hours’ notice is given before the start of the original daily tour, the changed tour becomes the regular scheduled tour (basic wage plus applicable premiums); if less than 24 hours’ notice is given, minimum three days’ notice applies for changes affecting two or more tours on the posted weekly schedule (otherwise overtime is paid for hours worked outside the original tours during the succeeding three calendar days). Relief periods are provided: 15 minutes paid for as time worked near the middle of each tour session, and if employees work 2+ hours immediately before/after the originally scheduled tour they receive a 15-minute relief period near each two-hour interval (where they resume work after each relief). Employees indicating availability for overtime/call-out must sign and manage an Availability List, and while the Company is not required to call those not on the list, absence from the list does not remove the employee’s overall responsibility to work overtime/call-out when offered. The contract also addresses holiday/week scheduling constraints (e.g., regular non-holiday scheduling limits of 32 hours per week unless service requires more; holiday work paid at a premium and counted for overtime calculations), compensated availability for after-hours critical/emergency services that rotates by seniority with seniority/volunteer rules and begins/ends on calendar years, and additional scheduling flexibility such as mutually agreed flexible work weeks (no overtime until after 40 hours) and part-time schedules assigned at Management’s discretion, with return to full-time at the end of approved voluntary part-time assignments.

Leave-related provisions cover (i) notice/authorization for inability to work and disciplinary consequences (employees unable to work scheduled hours due to sickness, injury, emergency, or circumstances beyond their control must give the maximum possible notice to their supervisor/office; failure may result in discipline), (ii) personal holidays (regular employees may select and observe personal holidays anytime in the 12 months of the calendar year with at least 30 days’ notice; supervisory waivers are possible; if a selected day is unavailable or multiple employees in the same work group select the same day, alternatives are chosen by seniority; normally taken as paid day(s) off; with supervisory approval personal holidays may be taken in 4-hour increments and one personal holiday in minimum 2-hour increments; one personal holiday may be carried over if scheduled by January 1 and taken no later than the week beginning with the last Sunday in March; Verizon Plus employees recognize an additional personal holiday in lieu of the day after Thanksgiving, and effective 1/1/2003 regular employees are eligible for a 6th personal holiday; designated holidays observed on Saturday are observed on the preceding Friday unless the employee is scheduled to work Saturday, and Sunday holidays are observed the following Monday; “holiday” is a 24-hour period from 12:01 A.M. to midnight); and (iii) holiday pay/limitations (regular full-time employees are paid their hourly rate for 8 hours on each holiday/day observed; regular part-time employees are paid based on an average prior representative workday schedule, with additional holiday allowance for hours worked in excess of schedule; holiday allowance generally is not paid for absences during specified portions of the duty day before/after the holiday or when an employee fails to work a scheduled holiday, unless authorized for justifiable circumstances; employees should, where practical, be excused from work on holidays); plus related absence/leave administration (excused time must be authorized by management; for absences exceeding 3 consecutive scheduled days, the company may require a physician report and unsubstantiated illness/injury beyond 3 days is ineligible for short-term disability; employees cannot receive short-term disability benefits for time already paid by other benefits; employees may elect, with supervisory approval, to offset scheduled sickness-disability lost time by using earned day-at-a-time vacation and/or personal holiday(s)); and broader leave of absence rules (management may grant informal leaves up to 30 calendar days, formal leaves beyond 30 days per company rules; remaining away beyond the leave term or taking other employment during the leave can lead to discharge; jury duty and witness time off are paid at straight-time for scheduled lost time under conditions stated; death-in-immediate-family allows up to 3 days paid time off selected within a specified window with a defined “immediate family” list; union leave requires 15 days’ notice, limits on total days and number of employees at any time, no less than one working day per leave, and special consideration for union officers with limits; employees performing contract negotiations have lost time excluded from vacation eligibility with maximum notification; military training/service leaves are granted with continued accredited service and reinstatement conditions; and FMLA is addressed with up to 12 work weeks within a 12-month period, concurrent running with other qualifying CBA-provided leave, eligibility limits, documentation requirements (medical certification within 25 days of request or denial may result), advance notice when foreseeable, spouse/household limitations on combined FMLA for the same circumstance, intermittent/reduced schedules only as medically necessary/approved as provided, and restrictions against accepting other employment or unemployment benefits while on leave).

Healthcare-related provisions include short-term disability and related exclusions (regular employees may receive disability payments at basic rates for scheduled work days missed due to illness or physical injury, with an instruction to notify the GTE Short Term Disability Administrator immediately for absences beyond three consecutive scheduled work days; disability benefits are not available for work time lost due to mental/emotional illness, drug addiction, and/or alcoholism unless disability is determined by a licensed psychiatrist, except hospitalization and/or intensive outpatient therapy). The Company provides a voluntary Group Health Insurance Plan at group rates via payroll deductions, with Company premium contributions equal to 100% of the participating employee’s individual coverage, employee+one dependent, or family monthly premium for full-time employees (and for certain part-time employees hired before January 1, 1991); for part-time employees hired after January 1, 1991, Company pays 100% monthly for individual and 50% for employee+one dependent or family. Coverage eligibility for medical (and dental, as an independent offering effective 7-1-2000) begins after 90 days of employment or upon enrollment, whichever is later. Dental includes a $25.00 per-individual deductible waived when an employee/dependents use a Preferred Dental Provider. Additional medical benefits include a hearing aid benefit added to the medical plan with a $1,000 maximum reimbursement per covered individual every 24 months (no deductible/co-pays/R&C), and prescriptions through a Mail Order Prescription Plan extended effective 7-1-2003 (not available for HMO/POS participants). Point of Service and Prescription Identification Card provisions set administration/discretion by the Company and permit use only under specified plan limits (e.g., prescription network copayment/ deductible rules and that PIC/MOPP are not available for HMO/POS participants). Vision coverage is implemented effective 7-1-2003, is automatic with enrollment in Verizon medical options (waiver of medical coverage waives vision), and is Company-paid. The contract also provides medical coverage at no charge for eligible surviving spouses, dependents, and registered domestic partners for 24 months after an active employee’s death, an annual $500 “opt out” credit (if the employee/dependents are not enrolled in the Company medical plan or an HMO), FMLA leave maintenance of company-paid life/medical/dental benefits to the extent provided to active employees, and administration/carrier selection rights retained by the Company.

Ancillary provisions include: (i) a 50% employee concession on monthly recurring flat-rate local service network charges or USS basic local service and usage charges (including touch calling) and applicable state/federal excise taxes for regular employees with at least six months of accredited service, excluding access charges for residence telephone service; all toll, foreign exchange, non-recurring, installation/repair, moves/changes, and other services are at regular rates; and (ii) employee benefit-related ancillary plans and reimbursements, including adoption assistance with reimbursement of expenses incurred on/after July 1, 2003 up to $10,000 per adopted child, and a Flexible Reimbursement Plan (North Central Region). The Hourly Savings Plan (HSP) is made available to covered regular full/part-time hourly employees (effective/subject to terms), can be terminated or partially terminated by the Board at any time (with nonforfeitable member accounts if terminated/partially terminated or contributions cease), and may only be merged/consolidated/transferred if members receive benefits at least equal to those immediately prior; HSP revisions are contingent on maintaining qualified status under Internal Revenue Code Section 401(a) et seq. Company matching contributions to the HSP increase to 66¢ per $1 (effective July 1, 2000) up to 6% of pay, then 75¢ per $1 (effective July 6, 2003) and 82¢ per $1 (effective July 4, 2004), each up to 6% of pay. Additional ancillary cash allowance terms include an ISP Expense Allowance (not to exceed $750 per completed year, maximum $3,750 pre-tax, not prorated) for employees leaving service with ISP benefits, over and above an ISP termination allowance. Ancillary retiree/post-termination insurance includes retiree life insurance of $5,000 for employees retiring on/after July 1, 1997 and $10,000 for employees retiring on/after July 1, 2003, each for those with service or disability pension under the GTE Pension Plan. Finally, employees covered by the collective bargaining agreement are given ancillary opportunities to purchase automobile, home and other personal property/casualty insurance via payroll deduction effective July 1, 2000, and participation rules for a Public Communications Incentive Compensation Plan provide awards for retirements/disability/death during the plan year through earned amounts up to the effective date and payment of all awards earned if employment terminates before scheduled payout.

Security-related provisions in the agreement primarily address employment protections and access tied to seniority, service/credited service, and recall/transfer rights. Specifically, employees are subject to probationary rules (90 days, extendable by mutual agreement up to an additional 90 days; probation for wage progression transfers to a higher classification not to exceed 180 calendar days), and credited service is managed through documentation (a maintained seniority file by department) and bridging after 1,000 hours of credited service. In force reduction/layoff situations, employees retain accumulated accredited service unless the layoff continues beyond 24 consecutive months, may elect termination with termination allowance, volunteer for layoff with recall rights, or exercise job transfer/bumping rights if they have more than 12 months accredited service (with additional distance/eligibility limits, including forfeiture of bumping/recall rights for certain refused transfers within 25 miles). Recall rights include detailed notice and response timing (conclusive receipt after mailing; notify availability within 3 days and report within 10 days, with sickness/injury exceptions allowing continued rights if notice and evidence are provided), and recall placement must respect credited service order by classification/district and may require placement on the appropriate wage progression. Employees returned following force reduction can reenter the prior classification and location (subject to wage schedule rules, with a right limited to two years and the requirement to desire retransfer). Additionally, contingent and voluntary layoff leave frameworks limit durations (e.g., contingent employment not to exceed 12 consecutive months; voluntary layoff leave not to exceed four months) and preserve accredited service/seniority during the leave and reinstatement protections at return.

The Company will make reasonable efforts, consistent with telephone service requirements, to train and promote existing employees, but this will not override job awards to laid-off employees; when “Ready Now” vacancies arise due to management needing more experienced personnel than available within the unit, or when openings are filled under Article 6, Section 6.10, the Business Manager must be advised ten (10) days before filling. The Company and Union will continue joint educational efforts, including 100% tuition reimbursement and 100% prepaid features, and may form joint study teams (management and union officials) on an “as needed” basis to develop joint educational programs. For the Equipment Installer Assistant (a developmental, workforce-augmentation role), employees are automatically awarded the higher central office based COE Installer-Repairer classification if their accredited Equipment Installer Assistant service exceeds twenty-four (24) consecutive months and they complete all required training, prerequisite testing, and performance requirements; such employees receive no more than two (2) opportunities to pass the prerequisite COE Installer-Repairer testing, with unsuccessful outcomes governed by item 4 (not included here). Equipment Installer Assistant and Network Assistant employees may not bid on other opportunities (except force adjustment), and, after completing required training/testing/performance, the COE Installer-Repairer position is awarded with the location set by the Company with employee input based on availability and service needs. During the Agreement term, the Company may notify the Union in writing of technological changes that create or will create a surplus, making eligible regular employees eligible for Plan participation (details not provided here). Network Assistant placements are set to Wage Schedule N-8, require appropriate Verizon-determined testing, and are filled under Article 8 job application procedures.

The contract’s grievance/dispute procedure requires that disputes raised by employees or the Union be presented to Management on the Union’s forms (or orally at the outset) stating relevant details (names, dates/times/events), the contract provisions allegedly violated, and the remedy sought; technical form errors cannot bar the grievance. For oral grievances, notice must be given to the employee’s Supervisor within seven days (excluding Sunday) of the event, or within seven days after the matter first became known, but in any case within 45 days of the event. If not settled within five (5) working days after submission to the Supervisor, the grievance must be filed in writing within seven (7) days (excluding Sunday) to the second-level Manager; a meeting occurs within five (5) working days unless waived by mutual agreement, and the Union receives a written response within seven (7) working days, with copies forwarded as specified. If still unresolved, Step 2 requires submission to the Regional Director/Labor–Employee Relations (or designee) within eight (8) days (excluding Sunday) after the first-step hearing date, with a meeting within seven (7) working days unless waived and a written response within fourteen (14) working days after the second-step hearing; employees and one Union representative are paid their basic hourly rates for scheduled work hours spent at Steps 1 and 2. Management may not discuss a grievance with the aggrieved employee without the appropriate Union representative once a Union representative has presented the grievance. If the dispute remains unresolved after fourteen (14) working days following the second-step hearing, either party may request arbitration by serving a written demand within thirty (30) days (excluding Sundays), with arbitrator selection within ten (10) days (excluding Sunday) of notice; each party bears its own presentation costs, and arbitrator/incidental costs agreed in advance are split equally. The agreement also permits oral complaint/adjustment while preserving the employee’s right to Union representation during the oral complaint and adjustment, and allows Union mediation (for specified discipline and sickness disability benefit grievances) with the Union participant attendance paid if held during the employee’s scheduled tour. Multiple benefit/plan-related matters are explicitly excluded from the CBA grievance/arbitration procedure (e.g., Adoption Assistance Plan, FRP, HSP, Living Benefit Rider, MOPP, Incentive Compensation Plan, and certain trust/retiree medical benefit administration disputes), while disputes about whether plan pay is made per plan terms remain subject to the grievance (and arbitration) process; the Company also has sole discretion for various excluded plan determinations and corresponding dispute resolutions.

Safety-related provisions include reaffirming nondiscrimination and fair treatment (race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, handicap/disabled veteran status, age, and Vietnam Era veteran status); requiring pre-employment (and after an absence of more than three months) physical examinations by a Company-approved physician; limiting outdoor construction/maintenance by certain department employees during heavy rain, wet snow, or excessively cold weather unless necessary to protect life, property, or essential services (with alternative work assigned when scheduled work is suspended); and allowing compensation for employees who cannot safely report to work due to severe weather if specified conditions are met. The Company retains investigatory rights for disability claims and may require a second physician opinion at Company expense. The Company must furnish necessary tools and safety items at no cost (including replacement of broken/worn tools due to normal use; replacement of lost/stolen tools at the employee’s expense except for loss beyond the employee’s control, such as failure to provide secure storage; and condemnation of unsafe/unfit tools), and provides work gloves for outside plant forces subject to the tool provisions. Employees are responsible for safe vehicle operation and for reporting vehicle defects, tool/supply shortages, and unsafe tools/equipment in writing to appropriate supervisors. The agreement also requires strict adherence to health and safety measures for employees and the public, continuous education and compliance efforts on safe practices, and quarterly safety meetings (with two union-designated employees paid at basic hourly rates for regular scheduled meeting hours). Finally, the Company has exclusive responsibility to provide a safe and healthful workplace, and DOT-required random drug testing is at the Company’s cost (with confidentiality, documentation of observations, retesting/second specimen procedures within ten (10) work days, limits on unannounced testing beyond one year post-treatment, and employee rights to discuss test results).

Miscellaneous provisions include: employees assigned more than 60 miles from their regular reporting center may charge the Company one 5-minute personal long-distance call terminating in Ohio per day (with written form notice); if they do not return home on interim weekends, they are reimbursed $8.00 per week starting with the second week of the temporary assignment. Moving to a new location costs are assumed by the employee. No termination allowance is due where termination results from retirement on pension, death, transfer between companies, resignation/quit, dismissal for cause, or as a result of a sale/other disposition of the exchange/office where the employee continues under new management. Telephone service at the employee’s residence with listing in the employee’s name qualifies for concession rates. The Union agrees to indemnify the Company for claims arising from the Company’s good-faith application of specified provisions, and the Union also agrees not to intimidate/coerce or interfere with bargaining-unit work, nor to engage in or cause strikes or work slowdowns during the Agreement (with violations subject to immediate discharge). The Company agrees not to lock out or shut down for anti-Union purposes, and must provide Union bulletin boards (max. 15" x 18") for approved Union notices only, with unapproved postings causing removal of the bulletin board for the Agreement’s duration. Employment benefits not otherwise provided may not be diminished during the Agreement term except by prior Union agreement. Related miscellany also provides for permission, where practical, to take a Company vehicle home when assigned “Compensated Availability” (with reasonable care; vehicle/tools not for personal use), various administrative/notice items (e.g., employees designated “Contingent” on occupational titles; split-specimen testing with retest availability and reimbursement if the second test is negative; specified consent-form deletion; and hold-harmless indemnity re the Drug and Alcohol Policy), and additional language ensuring employees/domestic partners notify the Company of changes to stated conditions.
